subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the value of k if the angle between the straight lines 4x−y+7=0, kx−5y−9=0 is 45°.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.62 — SAQ chapter 9 The Straight Line, answer 57. Printed appearances: TS M-17 · AP M-16. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. steps.margin_note: First mark. Read both slopes off the coefficients as −a/b. The second carries the unknown, which the angle condition will then find.

steps.label: Write the angle formula
steps.margin_note: The next two marks. The angle between two lines is tanθ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)|. At 45° the tangent is 1, so the modulus equals 1.

steps.why: The modulus stands for two equations. They give two different second lines, one turned 45° each way from 4x − y + 7 = 0, so both values of k are answers — dropping one loses half of what the question asks for.

steps.label: Solve both branches
steps.margin_note: The last three marks. Solve each branch separately and report both values.

and 5 to the right: 3k = −25; divide by 3)

steps.why: The ± gives two different second lines: one turned 45° one way from 4x − y + 7 = 0, the other turned 45° the other way. Each really does make a 45° angle with the given line, so both values of k are correct answers, not a sign of error.
common_mistakes: Sign slip when distributing the minus over (20 − k).
steps.memory_tip: Solve each branch separately and report BOTH values.

insider_note: With tan 45° = 1 the formula becomes |5 + 4k| = |20 − k|, and removing the modulus gives TWO equations. Solving both carries the last three of the eight marks, so write both k = 3 and k = −25/3.
